findings.note: This ESPN page is for ALCS Game 2, with Cleveland up 1-0. It lists Freddy Peralta (postseason: 1.93 ERA, 0.86 WHIP) against Parker Messick (5.40 ERA, 1.80 WHIP, 6 BB in 6.2 IP). It shows TB at about -137, ESPN's predictor gives CLE 40.5, and it lists no new injuries to key players.

Cleveland came from behind to beat ace Drew Rasmussen and the favored Rays 7-3 in Game 1. That makes four straight wins for the Guardians, and José Ramírez is hot. To note: Cleveland used five relievers plus closer Cade Smith, which could tire its bullpen for Game 2.
This series preview describes a tired Guardians pitching staff against well-rested Rays, with four games in five days. Cleveland used only three starters in its ALDS, which went the full five games.

CBS's ALCS Game 1 live blog says Caminero went down clutching near his chest after colliding with Jonny DeLuca but stayed in the game. Cleveland relievers Espino and Gaddis struck him out, and his only other noted hit was a first-inning RBI single, all one base.

MLB.com's Game 1 recap says Caminero avoided serious injury from the DeLuca collision and the spotlight moves to him in Game 2 Tuesday night. No Game 2 lineup or Cleveland starter was confirmed in the results.

In MLB.com's expert panel, 13 voters picked Caminero as ALCS MVP, more than anyone else. That is a series-level opinion, not a total bases pick, and it notes he hasn't homered yet this postseason despite 42 regular-season homers.
